title: kit.theme-sources.v1
description: Where each vendored diagram theme (packages/core/registry/themes/<key>.init) came from: the project key, the repository and path it was taken from, the upstream commit, and the git blob id (sha1 of "blob <length>\0<content>", what `git hash-object` prints) of the vendored file and of each font file it loads. A test recomputes every blob id, so a hand edit of a vendored file fails. The file is written by `kit diagrams themes --sync`, never by hand (docs/DIAGRAMS.md, "each organisation's own colours").

project.description: Registry key of the project; its entry in projects.json names the vendored file in `theme`.

via.description: copy: the file is a byte copy of the upstream docs/diagrams/theme.init at `path`. derive: the upstream has no usable theme.init, so the file is the output of `kit diagrams derive` on the upstream brand tokens at `path`. provisional: the project has no brand kit yet, so the file is a stand-in written in the kit and no upstream exists; it names no repo, path or commit, carries a `note` that says what it waits for, and is replaced by a copy once the project publishes its theme.init.

repo.description: owner/repo; one of the project's `github` repositories in projects.json (copy and derive).

path.description: The upstream file: its docs/diagrams/theme.init (copy) or its brand tokens module (derive).

commit.description: The upstream commit (origin/main of `repo`) the file was taken from.

blob.description: Git blob id of the vendored file.

fonts.description: The font files the theme's `%% font:` lines load, vendored beside it so a diagram of this project renders anywhere.

theme_path.description: The path in the theme's `%% font:` line (relative to the upstream repository).

file.description: The vendored font, relative to packages/core/registry/themes/.

source_blob.description: via derive: the git blob id of the source (the tokens file at path, at commit) the theme was derived from; blob is then the derived theme's own bytes

note.description: via provisional: why the theme is provisional and what it waits for (the owner's brand kit).
